Commentary.Commentary: We are all set for the game to restart for Australia's second-inning effort as the umpires make their way out to the middle. The Indian players are in a huddle near the boundary line and they are having a long chat before taking their respective positions on the field. Usman Khawaja and David Warner are already at the pitch and look eager to get going. Mohammad Shami has the new ball in his hand and is ready to begin proceedings. Let's play...
...  THIRD INNINGS ...

Australia have bowled India out for 296 and have taken a first-innings lead of 173 runs! Having started the day 318 runs behind, India lost KS Bharat early and were staring down the barrel. Shardul Thakur joined hands with Ajinkya Rahane and steadied the ship with a 109-run stand. It was a frustrating first session for Australia and they were expected to fight back in the second session. They surely did as Pat Cummins led from the front to dismiss Ajinkya Rahane early in the second session. After the departure of Rahane, Shardul Thakur had no other option to go for the big shots and he perished shortly after completing his fifty. Cameron Green and Mitchell Starc came to the party as well to run through India's tail.  Australia would have fancied a lead in excess of 200 but the lead of 173 runs is still a daunting one on this surface. On the other hand, this has been a good recovery by India and now need their bowlers to bowl exceptionally well in the second innings. Can the Indian bowlers replicate their counterparts? Let's find out as Australia's reply is coming up shortly...

Commentary.Commentary: All in readiness for the post-Lunch session to commence as the two umpires make their way out to the middle. Pat Cummins is seen giving final instructions to his group in the huddle. They now walk out to the centre followed by Ajinkya Rahane and Shardul Thakur. It will be Scott Boland to start with the ball in the second session. Let's play...
... DAY 3, SESSION 2 ...

As far as Australia are concerned, it was a frustrating session for them to say the least. They opted to start the proceedings with Scott Boland and it paid dividends straight away as the right-arm pacer dismissed KS Bharat with a peach. From the other end, Pat Cummins did trouble the Indian batters by hitting the hard lengths but was unlucky to get a wicket. To add to his misery, Green dropped a regulation catch to give Shardul Thakur a life early in his innings. As he did on Day 2, Cummins rotated his bowlers but none of them were able to find a breakthrough. In the last over before Lunch, Pat Cummins did trap Shardul Thakur in front of the stumps but he overstepped to give Thakur another life. Australia will need to regroup during this break and start afresh in the second session. Do join us back at 5.40 pm IST (12.10 pm GMT) for what promises to be another exciting session of Test cricket.

SESSION SUMMARY - 109 runs, 22 overs, 1 wicket. As the two teams head into Lunch on Day 3, it has been India's batting depth that has come to their rescue and it will be India who will be the happier of the two sides. Having begun Day 3 in a precarious position, India were dealt an early blow, losing KS Bharat on the second ball of the day. Shardul Thakur made his way to the middle and found himself battered and bruised on the forearm courtesy of the variable bounce. That said, he showed immense composure and offered great support to his partner. India's man of crisis, Ajinkya Rahane stepped up when his team wanted him to and now finds himself 11 runs short of the three-figure mark. Both batters did have their fair share of luck in the session but credit must be given where it's due. The duo have stitched a 108-run stand to keep India in the game and will look to take India closer to parity in the upcoming session of play.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set for the commencement of Day 3, the moving day of a Test match as the umpires make their way out to the middle. The Australian players are in a huddle beyond the boundary before following the umpires out and taking their respective positions on the field. Ajinkya Rahane and KS Bharat have a massive job in hand if they are to save India the blushes. Scott Boland will bowl the first over of the morning and is ready to begin proceedings. Let's play...

PITCH REPORT - Nasser Hussain is pitchside and he says that the weather is excellent. The temperature on Day 3 will be between 19 to 24 degrees with a 0% chance of rain which is much hotter than it was on Day 2 and will get warmer as we enter the weekend. Mentions that in the first two days, they have seen uneven bounce with the ball rapping batters on the gloves and beating the bat which is odd to see so early in an Oval Test match. He is joined by Dinesh Karthik who informs that there are cracks that run straight down the pitch and that is what causes the uneven bounce. Claims that the delivery that got Virat Kohli's wicket hit either the indentations or one of the cracks. Reckons that there will definitely be spin on offer on this pitch and with the sun baking down, it is getting drier. Ends by saying that Nathan Lyon's wicket of Ravindra Jadeja is the first of many wickets by spinners we will see in this game.

After failing to make a mark with the ball on Day 1, Indian bowlers roared back on Day 2 and bowled Australia out for 469. In reply, Rohit Sharma and Shubman Gill got India off to a positive start. However, the Indian batters fell prey to errors in judgement and were soon reduced to 71-4. Ajinkya Rahane and Ravindra Jadeja forged a solid recovery, but Jadeja's departure before Stumps put them in a hole once again. A lot will rest on the shoulders of Ajinkya Rahane, and he will require support from the lower order. Can he bail India out of trouble? Let's find out, as action on Day 3 is coming up shortly.

For Australia, Steven Smith and Travis Head picked up where they left off and consolidated their side's position. Australia did lose their way a bit, but Alex Carey played a handy cameo to help his side stretch the first-inning total. Pat Cummins and Co. showed exceptional control with the ball and kept troubling the Indian batters. Australia would want to make good use of the early movement on Day 3 and run through India's lower order to take a healthy first-innings lead.

Hello and a warm welcome, ladies and gentlemen, to our coverage of Day 3 of the 2021–23 World Test Championship final between Australia and India at the Kennington Oval in London. Having dominated the Test with the bat on Day 1, Australia backed it up with the ball on Day 2 and have a firm grip on the final after two days of play.
... DAY 3, SESSION 1 ...

Another day goes to Australia and they will now look to ascertain their claim to the title on Day 3 which is the moving day of the Test match. To be fair, we had ample movement on Day 2 as the Indian batters could not complement the good work done by their bowlers and are looking to be sinking deeper into the sand pit. They need a rope to hang onto here and the Aussies have not given them an inch. The action continues on Friday 9th June for Day 3 of this ultimate Test match and the first ball will be bowled at 3 pm IST (9.30 am GMT) but do join us early for the build-up. Cheers!

Scott Boland is in for a flash interview. He says that it is really exciting to play in the World Test Championship final and adds he had a nervous past couple of days. Mentions that it was nice to knock Shubman Gill over. Hopes that they can pick more wickets in the morning. Feels that they are in a really strong position after two days. Shares that the pitch is playing up and down with few balls taking off while few have kept low as well.

Australia came into Day 2 in a comfortable position and looked to be well on course to post a mammoth total on the board. Steven Smith took 2 deliveries to reach his century and Travis Head soon after got to his 150. After a decent start, the Aussies began losing wickets in a bundle as Mohammed Siraj dismissed Head for 163 and Cameron Green could not contribute with the bat. India made the morning session theirs when Shardul Thakur got Steven Smith to chop the ball onto the stumps and Mitchell Starc got run out taking a risky run. The Aussies still had 422 runs on the board going into the Lunch break having lost 7 wickets and would have still been aiming to get to the 500-run mark. Ravindra Jadeja picked up his first wicket of the game in the second session when he dismissed Alex Carey just short of his half-century and Mohammed Siraj added the finishing touches by dismissing Nathan Lyon and Pat Cummins with Australia scoring 469 runs in the first inning. Rohit Sharma and Shubman Gill started well but lost their wickets before going in for Tea and never looked like they would recover from it in the final session. Australia will be proud of the efforts as all the five bowlers they have used so far have claimed one wicket each.

SESSION SUMMARY - 114 runs, 28 overs, 3 wickets. Australia have consolidated their position in this game as they are staring at a massive first-inning lead. They had India in all sorts of trouble at the Tea break having dismissed both their openers with the scoreboard reading 30 and would have been looking to start this final session well. They opted to go with Cameron Green from one side and he justified their faith in him by claiming the crucial wicket of Cheteshwar Pujara who did not offer a shot and saw his off pole destroyed. Mitchell Starc did not look to be in good rhythm but just as he has done so often in the past bowled an absolute jaffa to dismiss Virat Kohli who was looking determined at the wicket. India suddenly found themselves 71 for the loss of four wickets till Ravindra Jadeja came out with positive intent and scored 48 runs in 51 deliveries. He added 71 runs in 100 balls with Ajinkya Rahane but fell to the guile of Nathan Lyon close to Stumps. Rahane got a lifeline when Pat Cummins caught him in front of the stumps but overstepped the bowling crease and he holds the flame of hope for India at the moment. With India still trailing by 318 runs, Australia have a great opportunity to attack them in the morning session of Day 3.

Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the post-Tea session on Day 2. The Australian players are seen in a huddle near the ropes. Virat Kohli and Cheteshwar Pujara make their way out to the centre and they are joined by the Australian players. Scott Boland will start the proceedings with the ball for Australia. Off we go...
... DAY 2, SESSION 3 ...

There is plenty of enticing action coming our way in the last session of Day 2 and Australia have a great opportunity to stake their claim for a win in this game by taking a bunch of wickets early after the break. India need to believe that Day 2 and Day 3 are the best days to bat in England and will want to use these conditions to set up a fightback even though the Aussie pace bowlers have their tails up. Do join us at 8 pm IST (2.30 pm GMT) to find out how the post-Tea session plays out…

Australia would have liked Alex Carey and their skipper Pat Cummins to build a partnership and take them through to Tea but Carey was dismissed two runs short of his half-century ending a 51-run partnership. Nathan Lyon showed some resistance at the crease but saw his stumps shattered and Pat Cummins was the last wicket to fall in his quest to get some quick runs. They would have wanted to post a total above 500 and would be disappointed with their batting effort on Day 2 but what would have worried them more is that there was no help for their pace bowlers early on. They allowed the Indian batters to get off to a good start with some poor deliveries till Cummins produced a peach of a delivery to trap the Indian skipper in front of the stumps. Things got better for them when Scott Boland sent the other opener back to the shed by pegging his off pole back and now find themselves in a commanding position in the game.

SESSION SUMMARY - 84 runs, 22.3 overs, 5 wickets. Having done extremely well to bowl their opponents out, India have dug themselves into a hole with the bat! They went into the post-Lunch session with Australia batting on 422 for the loss of 7 wickets and did extremely well to bowl them out within the first hour with 47 runs added to the total. The pace bowlers were not able to get the breakthrough but the introduction of Ravindra Jadeja helped them break the eighth-wicket partnership that was building. Mohammed Siraj cleaned the tail up before drinks could be taken, following which the Indian openers came out to bat showing positive intent. Just when they seemed to be looking comfortable at the wicket, both Rohit Sharma and Shubman Gill were dismissed in consecutive overs to give the initiative back to the Australians. They now have an uphill task to climb to save this game and will be heavily reliant on Cheteshwar Pujara and Virat Kohli to do the bulk of the scoring as they still trail by 432 runs.
